output.reason: A few weeks of intermittent post-fatty-meal right upper quadrant pain without reported fever or jaundice suggests possible gallstone disease needing clinician-arranged assessment and likely ultrasound, but no reported feature requires emergency or same-day care.
output.patientMessage: Please start a message review with a Counsel clinician in this thread in the next few days; recurring right-upper-belly pain after fatty meals often points to gallstones, and a clinician can arrange an ultrasound and blood tests. Meanwhile, eat lower-fat meals. Seek emergency care now if pain becomes severe and constant beyond a few hours, or you develop fever, chills, vomiting, or yellow eyes or skin.
differential: Peptic ulcer or reflux-related upper abdominal pain
